title: Artinian length-one lifting produces sections of truncated quotients
statement: Let R and A be commutative rings in Type u with an R-algebra structure on A, q a prime ideal of A, S = A_q [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and C a Noetherian local commutative R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with a surjective R-algebra map C -> S. Set J = ker(C -> S) and m the unique maximal ideal of C. Assume that for every surjective ring map phi : B' -> B of Artinian local commutative rings in Type (max u v), whose kernel has B'-module length one [def-weil-pbc-module-length], and maps rho : R -> B' and a : A -> B such that a composed with R -> A equals phi composed with rho and the preimage under a of the maximal ideal of B is q, there is a ring map a' : A -> B' satisfying phi composed with a' = a and a' composed with R -> A = rho. Then for every integer N >= 1, the canonical R-algebra quotient map C/(J^2 + m^N) -> C/(J + m^N) has an R-algebra section. The R-algebra structures on both quotients are induced from C.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 02HT (lemma-smooth-test-artinian), proof of (4) implies (1); online text at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02HT read 2026-10-13

proof.text: The surjection C -> S pulls the maximal ideal of S back to m and maps m onto it. Therefore J is contained in m. For N >= 1 the ideals J^2 + m^N and J + m^N lie in m and contain m^N. Apply the Noetherian local quotient Artinian lemma to obtain nonzero Artinian local rings E and F. The canonical surjection E -> F has square-zero kernel, and F is S/n^N, so A -> F pulls the maximal ideal back to q.

Filter K = ker(E -> F) by ideals with length-one successive quotients, using exists_ideal_filtration_length_one. For 0 = K_0 <= ... <= K_r = K, the kernel of E/K_i -> E/K_(i+1) is K_(i+1)/K_i. Its length over E/K_i equals its length over E, since restriction along the surjective map identifies submodule lattices. The quotients are nonzero Artinian local since each K_i lies in the maximal ideal. Descending induction applies hlift at each step, preserving R compatibility and inverse image maximal ideal q, and yields A -> E over R.

The lift A -> E pulls the maximal ideal back to q. The local ring unit criterion makes every element outside q a unit in E, so localization extends the map to S. This extension maps n into the maximal ideal of E, whose N-th power vanishes. It therefore factors through S/n^N = F. Composing the factor with E -> F gives the identity: it agrees on A, hence on S by localization uniqueness and then on F by surjectivity. Thus it is an R-algebra section.

Transport each Artinian quotient used for hlift to Type (max u v) by ULift ring equivalences. Surjectivity, local and Artinian structures, length and commuting equations are preserved, and the lifts transport back. N = 1 and J = 0 give identity quotient maps.

theorem artinian_lifting_truncated_section
    {R A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime]
    (P : Extension.{u} R (Localization.AtPrime q))
    [IsLocalRing P.Ring] [IsNoetherianRing P.Ring]
    (hlift : ∀ (B' B : Type (max u v)) [CommRing B'] [CommRing B]
      [IsArtinianRing B'] [IsArtinianRing B] [IsLocalRing B'] [IsLocalRing B]
      (φ : B' →+* B), Function.Surjective φ → Module.length B' (RingHom.ker φ) = 1 →
      ∀ (ρ : R →+* B') (a : A →+* B),
        a.comp (algebraMap R A) = φ.comp ρ →
          Ideal.comap a (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) = q →
        ∃ a' : A →+* B', φ.comp a' = a ∧ a'.comp (algebraMap R A) = ρ) :
    ∀ (N : ℕ), 1 ≤ N →
      ∃ σ : (P.Ring ⧸ (P.ker ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal P.Ring ^ N)) →ₐ[R]
          (P.Ring ⧸ (P.ker ^ 2 ⊔ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal P.Ring ^ N)),
        (Ideal.Quotient.factorₐ R
          (sup_le_sup (Ideal.pow_le_self (by decide : 2 ≠ 0)) le_rfl)).comp σ =
            AlgHom.id R _
